coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: The Stack (Unit 3 smokestack)
record.summary: A 300-foot concrete boiler exhaust stack built in 1965 alongside the Unit 3 Power Block; explicitly retained as an existing structure under the Design for Development, and slated to anchor a temporary art installation within the interim Prequel Park.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- Figure 6.2.3 marks this with a single point symbol and the label 'STACK / EXISTING STRUCTURE (~300')', not a footprint outline, but this polygon has been rebuilt 2026-09-16 (second pass) to trace the structure's actual visible footprint in satellite imagery (a fallen/lowered stack lying on the ground) rather than a diagram-derived placeholder. Treat as accurate to roughly 5-10m -- limited mainly by how precisely the lon/lat grid overlay could be read against the image, not by diagram-transform error.
notes.digitized_from: Potrero Power Station Design for Development, Figure 6.2.3 - Building Height Plan (p.245).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: This is an existing structure without its own subdivided Assessor parcel -- it sits within the larger, largely unaddressed former power-station site.
notes.regulatory_context: The historic ~300 ft tall smokestack from the power station's Unit 3 generating block, explicitly called out on the D4D's own Figure 6.2.3 as an 'Existing Structure' the plan retains (unlike the rest of the demolished power block) -- a literal, physical landmark left standing amid the redevelopment, sitting within Block 9's mapped development envelope (see potrero_block_9.geojson) at the site's waterfront edge. The Block 9 Building Configurations inset on the same figure shows two alternate massing options labeled 'WITH UNIT 3' and 'WITHOUT UNIT 3' -- suggesting the adjacent Unit 3 power block building (distinct from the Stack itself) may or may not be retained; the diagram does not draw Unit 3's own footprint distinctly enough to trace separately, so it is not mapped here as its own feature.

facts.value: 300 ft (described in the DEIR as a '300-foot tall concrete boiler exhaust stack'; the D4D final and SF Planning's project page both cite the existing structure at approximately 300 ft)

Contributor to the Third Street Industrial District (added when the district's period of significance was extended to 1965); not individually evaluated as eligible under a separate criterion in the source reviewed

Retained as an 'Existing Structure' under the Design for Development; the height limit for the Stack is fixed at its existing height and does not carry over to a replacement structure if the Stack is destroyed
Proposed to be opened as a temporary art gallery within Prequel Park

open_questions: The Chronicle (May 2025) describes the stack as 'built in 1962'; the DEIR's own historic-resources table (2018, citing a 2008 State DPR district record) dates both the Boiler Stack and the Unit 3 Power Block to 1965. This dossier uses the DEIR's dated figure and flags the Chronicle's 1962 claim as unreconciled, not necessarily wrong.

No source found confirming whether the temporary art-gallery use inside the Stack has an approved permit or a target opening date beyond the general Prequel Park timeline (see the Prequel Park records).
No source found on the Stack's structural condition, ownership of the underlying land parcel, or any historic landmark designation beyond 'contributor' status.
